 Kirkland Whipped Cream Recalled at Costco in 12 States Over Possible Cleaning Chemical Before Thanksgiving
 Published Nov 15, 2026 10:12 AM EST 
 By
 Joseph James 
 RDNE Stock project | Pexels 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 Costco shoppers in 12 states who bought Kirkland Signature Real Heavy Whipped Cream in October should check their refrigerators before Thanksgiving. Manufacturer Alamance Foods is voluntarily recalling one batch because it may contain a small amount of a cleaning chemical, ABC News reported .
 The recalled cans were sold between Oct. 11 and Oct. 31, 2026, at Costco warehouses in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Wisconsin. No serious adverse effects requiring medical care have been reported.
 The timing matters for families. Aerosol whipped cream is a holiday staple for pies, hot cocoa and coffee, and many households stock up weeks before Thanksgiving. A can bought in late October could easily still be in the fridge, waiting for dessert on Nov. 26.
 The Cans Included in the Recall
 The recall covers 15-ounce cans sold in three-packs and shipped in eight-count cases. Affected cans carry item code AC50 and a "best if used by" date of April 2, 2027, printed as APR/02/27. Costco's item number for the product is 1777000, Parade reported .
 Shoppers also need to check the time stamp printed on the can. Only cans stamped from 00:35 through 02:45 are included. A can with the same date but a time stamp outside that window is not part of the recall.
 Checking takes less than a minute, and it is worth doing even if the whipped cream looks and smells normal. Find the best-by date and time stamp printed on the can, then compare both against the recall details. If either one does not match, the can is not affected.
 The company said the issue involves one batch of product made for Costco's Kirkland Signature label. It has not said how many cans were in that batch or which cleaning chemical may be present.
 Reports of a Chemical Smell, but No Serious Illness
 The recall began after customers noticed something wrong. "Members have reported a chemical smell and taste, but no serious adverse effects requiring medical care have been reported," Alamance Foods said, as quoted by ABC7 .
 The company said it is acting "out of an abundance of caution," according to a report on the Nov. 7 member letter . The letter went to members who bought the product between Oct. 11 and Oct. 31.
 How the cans became contaminated has not been explained, and MedicalDaily did not find a federal enforcement notice for the recall at publication. The recall was communicated through the manufacturer and Costco.
 That leaves some uncertainty. The specific substance and its level are unknown, so the health risk cannot be precisely described. What is known is that the reports so far involve smell and taste, not injuries.
 Returning the Product and Getting a Refund
 Costco and Alamance are asking customers to stop using the affected whipped cream and return it to any local Costco for a full refund . Shoppers who did not receive a letter should still check any Kirkland whipped cream bought during the recall window.
 Anyone with questions about the product can contact Alamance Foods at customer.care@alamancefood.com, according to Parade.
 People who already used some of the product and feel fine do not need emergency care, based on what the company has reported. Anyone who notices symptoms after eating it , such as mouth or throat irritation, nausea or vomiting, can call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 for free, confidential guidance. Trouble breathing, swelling, or severe or persistent vomiting needs urgent medical care.
 Parents should keep recalled cans away from children until they can be returned and should not use them for baking or decorating in the meantime.
 Holiday Kitchens Can Avoid a Last-Minute Scramble
 Thanksgiving is less than two weeks away, and the recall arrives during one of the busiest grocery stretches of the year. Checking cans now gives families time to replace them, rather than discovering a problem while dessert is being served.
 Any dessert already topped with whipped cream from a recalled can should be thrown out rather than served. That includes pies or trifles made ahead and stored in the refrigerator.
 Households that keep several cans should check each one. Three-packs can be split across refrigerators, pantries, or a relative's house, and a single unchecked can is easy to miss.
 Shoppers who bought Kirkland whipped cream outside the Oct. 11 to Oct. 31 window, or outside the 12 states, are not affected by this recall. The recall also does not cover other Kirkland dairy products .
 The next development to watch is whether the company or federal regulators release more detail about the chemical involved. MedicalDaily will report any expansion of the recall or new health guidance before the holiday.

 Key Questions Answered
 What was recalled? One batch of Kirkland Signature Real Heavy Whipped Cream, 15-ounce cans sold in three-packs, with item code AC50.
 Why was it recalled? Alamance Foods said the batch may contain a small amount of a cleaning chemical after members reported a chemical smell and taste.
 Which states are affected? Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Wisconsin.
 How can I tell if my can is recalled? Look for a best-if-used-by date of APR/02/27 and a time stamp from 00:35 through 02:45.
 Has anyone gotten sick? No serious adverse effects requiring medical care have been reported, according to the company.
 How do I get a refund? Stop using the product and return it to any Costco for a full refund.
 What if I already ate some? Watch for symptoms. Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 for guidance, and seek urgent care for trouble breathing or severe vomiting.
